title: On the distances between the core center and other central parts of a tree
summary: Let $T$ be a tree. For a vertex $v\in V(T)$, the eccentric subtree number $ε_T(v)$ is defined as $ε_T(v)=\min\{f_T(v,u): u\in V(T)\}$ where $f_T(v,u)$ denotes the number of subtrees of $T$ containing both $v$ and $u$. A core vertex of $T$ is a vertex with the maximum eccentric subtree number, and the set of all the core vertices of $T$ is called the core center of $T$. The core center of $T$ consists of either a single vertex or two adjacent vertices.
